title: The Great Urban Transformation
abstract: This book emphasizes the centrality of cities in China's ongoing transformation. Based on fieldwork in twenty-four Chinese cities between 1996 and 2007, the author forwards an analysis of the relations between the city, the state, and society through two novel concepts: urbanization of the local state and civic territoriality. Urbanization of the local state is a process of state power restructuring entailing an accumulation regime based on the commodification of state-owned land, the consolidation of territorial authority through construction projects, and a policy discourse dominated by notions of urban modernity. Civic territoriality encompasses the politics of distribution engendered by urban expansionism, and social actors' territorial strategies toward self-protection. Findings are based on observations in three types of places. In the inner city of major metropolitan centers, municipal governments battle high-ranking state agencies to secure land rents from redevelopment projects, while residents mobilize to assert property and residential rights. At the urban edge, as metropolitan governments seek to extend control over their rural hinterland through massive-scale development projects, villagers strategize to profit from the encroaching property market. At the rural fringe, township leaders become brokers of power and property between the state bureaucracy and villages, while large numbers of peasants are dispossessed, dispersed, and deterritorialized; their mobilizational capacity is consequently undermined.

narrative:
Short impact summary

The Great Urban Transformation (2010), published by Oxford University PressOxford, has been cited 725 times — enough that OpenAlex puts it in the top 1% of works in its field and year.

Full narrative

The Great Urban Transformation by You-tien Hsing was published by Oxford University PressOxford in 2010. Conceptually, the work connects to Politics, Restructuring, Political science, Metropolitan area and State (computer science).

OpenAlex records 725 citations. That places it in the top 1% of works in its field and year of publication. Citations peaked in 2020 with 77 citing works. Notable citing venues include Urban Studies, Cambridge University Press eBooks and International Journal of Urban and Regional Research. The citing works include 529 journal articles, 123 book chapters and 12 preprints. They come from 40 countries, led by the United States, China and the United Kingdom.

Open Library reports a combined count of 2 reading logs and catalog editions. Its subject matter aligns with Sustainable cities and communities among the Sustainable Development Goals.
